scenes.headline: How a 1.7B model gets a million-token window
scenes.sub: Three window layers, then one full layer.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tinder! Spark-X2.6-1.7B is a small open model with a window of a million tokens. Here's how its layers keep the cache small.

scenes.label: The layout
scenes.text: Only one layer in four looks at the whole context. The other three look at the last 512 tokens, so the cache barely grows.
scenes.say: The idea: only one layer in four looks at the whole context. The other three see just the last five hundred and twelve tokens.

steps.say: The model is twenty-eight layers deep, built from seven identical blocks of four layers.
Three layers in each block only attend to the most recent five hundred and twelve tokens.
The fourth attends to everything before it, and it rotates its queries and keys with a very slow clock.

steps.label: Window layer
steps.say: In a window layer a token sees only a short band behind it, so the cache never holds more than the window.

steps.label: Full layer
steps.say: In a full layer a token sees every earlier token. These seven layers carry the long-range lookups, and they are the cache that grows.

scenes.title: KV cache at a million tokens, bf16
scenes.say: Counted from the config, a million tokens of cache is fourteen gibibytes in this layout, against fifty-six if every layer were full.

left.title: None
items: The template closes the think block first.
left.say: With none, the template closes the think block for the model before it starts.

right.title: Low and high
items: A system line names the effort.
right.say: With low or high, a line in the system prompt names the effort, and the model decides how long to think.

scenes.text: A hybrid layout makes a long window affordable in memory. Whether it is usable is a separate test.

recap: One full layer in every four
Thinking is set by the template
scenes.say: To recap: one full layer in four, a short window for the rest, and thinking set by the template.
